chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Husayn ibn Mus'ab said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three things for which there is no excuse for anyone: fulfilling the trust to the righteous and to the impious; kindness to parents whether they are righteous or impious; and keeping the promise to the righteous and to the impious.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three obligations in Shia Islam that apply to everyone regardless of the recipient's piety?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates three unconditional obligations—fulfilling trusts, honoring parents, and keeping covenants—emphasizing that the moral status of the recipient (whether righteous or impious) does not negate the duty. This underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *istiqra'* (comprehensive application), where the validity of the act relies on the actor's adherence to the command rather than the merit of the other party. The inclusion of 'parents' alongside general trusts highlights the unique, enduring nature of filial piety even if the parents are sinful, a key point in Shia family law.
